title: Metal emblem
description: An editable letter becomes a machined silver relief with directional highlights and a graphite surround.
useCase: Experiment with material light on a typographic mark without importing a 3D mesh.
interaction: Change the mark, move the light or hold it in place.
reducedMotion: The automatic light is held still; mark editing and direct lighting control remain.
limitations: A procedural glyph height mask produces a 2.5D surface, not extruded geometry. Native WebGL 1 falls back to the editable flat mark.
look: Heavy bevelled silver letter with polished highlights and a soft shadow on dark graphite, with small grey header text and outlined input and button.
motion: The light sways slowly on a sine while reflective bands drift across the relief; the pointer re-aims the light, a button freezes the loop, and typing re-renders the letter.
adapt: Lighting is the `metal` shader: `light` plus a `sin(time*.33)*.25` sway, with specular exponent and band frequency both `22.`; `update` rasterises `text` into a blurred 16-bit height map (`radius = 9`). Replace the mark and header; keep the `me-fallback` layer.
